rationale: Every later delta is measured against this number. If the pipeline cannot reproduce 0.6016 the harness is wrong and no subsequent result means anything.
expected_gain_derivation: Not an improvement attempt; a correctness precondition. Target validation primary 0.6016.

hypothesis: Replacing the pointwise FM with LightGBM lambdarank over the same five categorical fields, with training groups chunked to 6 consecutive rows per user to match the ~5.6-row valid lists, will beat the 0.6016 baseline substantially.
rationale: The metric is a within-user ordering metric but the baseline optimises independent per-impression logloss, so it spends capacity on calibrating absolute probabilities that are irrelevant once a user's rows are sorted. A pairwise lambdarank gradient only ever compares rows inside the same group, i.e. it directly optimises the quantity the metric reads. Chunking to 6 makes the training group length and the NDCG position discount match the evaluation list length instead of a 43.5-row list whose discount concentrates on the top few of a much longer tail. Trees also absorb the tab/dur_bucket interactions with video identity via categorical splits without needing the extra embedding capacity the organizers found useless.
expected_gain_derivation: [POINTWISE_BASELINE] says the loss/metric mismatch is untouched and [ORGANIZER_UNEXPLORED] ranks loss change first, so the largest untried structural lever is here. [GROUP_SHAPE_MISMATCH] (43.5 vs 5.6) plus [SHORT_EVAL_LISTS] means the training discount currently addresses a different problem than the one scored; fixing both loss and list length together typically moves a CTR-style ranking from an FM pointwise baseline by 0.02-0.05 in AUC-like terms. Against the 0.6016->0.8484 [CEILING] headroom of 0.247, a 13% capture is 0.032. Zero new feature blocks means no drift-rejection risk on this iteration.

block_justifications.base5: It is exactly the official baseline field set, so this spec isolates the structural change (model family + ranking loss + group shape) with no feature-block confound and no drift-check exposure.

hypothesis: Adding out-of-fold train-window item quality rates (video/author long-view rate, click rate, impression count) to the five base categoricals under a LightGBM pointwise model will beat the 0.6016 baseline by a clear margin.
rationale: base5 exposes video_id only as a high-cardinality categorical, which both FM embeddings (1.14M rows, capacity-limited per the organizers) and LightGBM's categorical splitter handle poorly; item_agg converts the same identity into a dense, well-estimated numeric prior for how often that video/author actually gets long-viewed. Because that prior varies across the items inside a single user's ~6-row impression list, it can directly reorder that list, unlike user-side aggregates. 99.9% of valid videos appear in train, so the encoding is populated almost everywhere it is needed, and OOF encoding keeps the training rows honest.
expected_gain_derivation: [ORGANIZER_CAPACITY_DEAD] plus my iteration 1 result (lambdarank+chunk6 on base5 = 0.60086, indistinguishable from 0.60141 given [SEED_NOISE] 0.0008) says the bottleneck with base5 is not the loss and not capacity but the representation: five raw IDs contain little that a learner can generalise from. [HIGH_COVERAGE] 99.9% means an item-level rate feature is defined on essentially every valid row, and [WITHIN_USER_RANKING] means it is a legitimate reorderer because item quality varies within a list. Item-rate priors are the single largest reliable feature in CTR-style ranking; against the 0.247 headroom to [CEILING] I put this at ~9% capture = 0.022, with downside risk that the drift check rejects the impression-count component under [EXPOSURE_REGIME_CHANGE].

block_justifications.base5: Keeps the official field set as the constant substrate so the measured delta is attributable to the single added block, and retains user_id x video_id identity which the organizers say already absorbs most learnable signal.
block_justifications.item_agg: The only block that turns the high-cardinality video/author identity into a dense generalisable long-view prior that varies within a user's list, which is the sole kind of quantity that can reorder it under [WITHIN_USER_RANKING].

hypothesis: LightGBM lambdarank with 6-row training groups over the five base fields PLUS explicit duration-bias features (log duration and the duration percentile rank within the user's list) will jump well above 0.6016.
rationale: long_view is a watch-completion label, so its base rate is dominated by how long the video is: short videos are trivially 'long-viewed' relative to their length and long videos are not. dur_bucket in base5 is a coarse categorical embedding of that; log-duration plus the WITHIN-USER percentile rank of duration is the same signal expressed as a continuous, list-normalised quantity, which is precisely the shape a within-user ranker can exploit. The percentile-rank feature is defined by the user's own list, so it is not user-constant and it directly encodes 'is this the short one in this slate?' -- the single strongest reorderer available given the label definition. Trees split on it monotonically; an FM cannot represent it at all.
expected_gain_derivation: [ORGANIZER_UNEXPLORED] lists duration-bias modelling as untouched, and my two runs so far show the two levers I did try are exhausted: loss change alone on base5 gave 0.60086 and item quality priors gave 0.59933, both inside or below [SEED_NOISE] of the 0.60141 baseline. That pattern says the binding constraint is that no current feature varies informatively within a ~6-item list; [WITHIN_USER_RANKING] and [USER_CONSTANT_NO_EFFECT] say only such features can move the score. Duration is the mechanical driver of a completion label, so I expect it to be the largest single non-identity signal. Headroom to [CEILING] is 0.247; I put this at ~6-7% capture = 0.016, well above the 0.002 the [CONVERGENCE_MECHANICS] window needs this iteration.
